page: Amazon Web Services m7a.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also demonstrate average tier performance. For specialized workloads, the CPU supports AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA extensions, resulting in average performance for database operations, static web serving, and medium-sized language model inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile suitable for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a standard density for general-purpose applications. The lack of bundled local storage requires reliance on external block storage, which should be factored into architectural designs. This instance is best suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations.
